content: Individuals living with HIV who also have drug-resistant tuberculosis (TB) require further research to optimize treatment strategies. Studies are necessary to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of newer antiretroviral (ARV) drugs used in first-line, second-line, or third-line regimens, particularly in the context of TB and HIV co-infection. Additionally, more data is needed on the use of corticosteroids in people with HIV who have low CD4 cell counts to prevent immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS). There is a need for improved long-term data on viral load suppression in individuals using efavirenz 400 mg formulations, especially among pregnant women and those requiring TB co-treatment, including regimens containing rifampicin. The pharmacokinetics and safety of alternative dosing of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) during TB co-treatment also require further investigation. Lastly, additional research is essential to understand the outcomes of treating co-infections of TB and histoplasmosis.
